about.title: Capitola Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Capitola is small — roughly 10,189 people — and when a death is sudden, the news reaches 41st Avenue and Bay Avenue before a family has had time to breathe. Public collision records for 2025 show 33 injury crashes and 38 people hurt in the city, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. Wrongful death claims arise from more than crashes: a fall at a rental, a medical error, a defective product. California law lets a spouse or domestic partner and children bring the claim first, with certain dependents and heirs next in line. Families generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less when a public agency such as a city or county is involved. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Capitola families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who works on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Capitola Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is far shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting an attorney in place early protects that timeline.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: A claim can cover funeral and burial costs, the income and support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. None of this comes out of your pocket up front — attorneys in our network work on contingency.

items.question: Capitola recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death cases don't happen here?
items.answer: No. Traffic is only one source of these claims. A death caused by a fall at a vacation rental near the village, a surgical mistake at a nearby hospital, or a faulty product used at home can all give rise to a wrongful death action, regardless of what the road statistics show in a given year.

items.question: What if the City of Capitola or Santa Cruz County is partly responsible?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity follow a much shorter process than the standard two-year deadline, and a formal government claim usually has to be filed first. That could apply if a poorly maintained sidewalk, signal, or public vehicle played a role. It is one of the main reasons to speak with an attorney quickly rather than waiting.

items.question: There is already a criminal case. Can we still file a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death action is a separate civil matter and does not depend on whether prosecutors bring charges or win a conviction. The civil case focuses on compensating the family for its losses, and it can move forward on its own timeline.
